Randers is a city in the Central Denmark Region that, in the context of the national Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) quality reports, serves as a benchmark for high-performing clinical efforts in acute abdominal care [^src1]. While the name refers to the geographical location, the context of the database's quality indicators specifically points to the hospital-level initiatives and outcomes achieved within the Randers area, rather than the administrative institution of Regionshospitalet Randers itself [^src1]. 

In the 2025 annual quality report, Randers is highlighted as a "best practice hospital" for Indicator 2, which measures the proportion of acute patients receiving a CT scan within two hours [^src1]. The facility is noted as a prime example of successful quality improvement, having achieved an increase of more than 20 percentage points in this metric over a two-year period [^src1]. Due to these significant gains, the report's authors recommend that knowledge exchange be implemented so that all Danish patients can benefit from the specific interventions and workflows developed in Randers [^src1]. This aligns with the broader national effort to reduce wait times, improve diagnostic certainty, and optimize treatment pathways for acute surgical patients through standardized, measurable indicators and cross-disciplinary collaboration.
